blocks.html: The Quick Flight Toolbar gets your drone in the air, brings it home, and stops it fast when something goes wrong. Here is the safe order to fly it.

slides.title: Find the Quick Flight Toolbar
slides.html: The toolbar sits at the top of the UAS menu after takeoff. From left: Set Altitude, Emergency Stop, Return To Home, Quick Task, Follow EUD/Recon, Mission Manager.

slides.title: Set your altitude
slides.html: Tap Set Altitude, drag the slider to the height you want, then tap Set Altitude to confirm. Read the height as AGL (above ground), HAL (above launch) or MSL (sea level).

slides.title: Take off
slides.html: On the ground the Set Altitude button shows a green GO circle, called Takeoff Now. Tap it and the drone launches and climbs to the altitude you set.

slides.title: Emergency Stop
slides.html: Tap Emergency Stop to kill the current task, then OK on the prompt. It cancels Quick Tasks, Routes and altitude moves but not manual stick control. WARNING: some aircraft drift or backtrack before stopping.

slides.title: Return to Home
slides.html: Tap Return To Home (button 3) for a short press to fly back to the launch point. Long-press it to open Home Position Follow Options so the drone tracks your moving position instead.

slides.title: Land and disarm in place
slides.html:
In the Set Altitude dialog, Land-Now brings the drone straight down where it hovers. Landing and disarm vary by platform:

  • DJI aircraft hover low and need the physical Ground Control Station (GCS) to land and disarm.
  • Some MAVLink aircraft will backtrack before landing.

slides.title: Reposition with Quick Task
slides.html: Tap Quick Task, then tap a point on the map. Choose Go Now to fly there at current height, or Orbit to circle it. The Selected Coordinate field lets you type exact coordinates.
